weather.tip: Rain is essentially certain tonight (98% chance) — carry an umbrella for your commute home and add extra time on Varthur, Gunjur and other waterlogging-prone stretches that are already congested this week.

around.headline: Lokayukta traps Central GST Superintendent taking ₹8 lakh bribe on camera in Bengaluru
around.summary: The officer was caught on video accepting the bribe, per NDTV. If any official at a government office hints that a cash 'processing fee' will speed up your file, that's a bribe demand you can report directly to the Lokayukta helpline rather than pay.

around.headline: 13-year-old boy abducted and murdered by neighbour in Bengaluru over education-loan debt
around.summary: A UK-returned techie neighbour allegedly kidnapped and killed the boy in a bid to pressure the child's father to clear a loan, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald. Karnataka's child helpline (1098) is the number to call if a child seems to be missing or at risk.

around.headline: Urgent repairs ordered on Gunjur-Varthur stretch as criticism mounts over 'quickfix' patchwork
around.summary: Authorities ordered emergency pothole fixes after this week's viral gridlock, but business leader Mohandas Pai criticised the GBA's patch job as inadequate, per Deccan Herald and Public TV; separately, the entire Bannerghatta Road is now slated for full white-topping, per The Hindu. Expect continued lane closures and delays on both corridors through the fixes.
around.source: Deccan Herald, Public TV, The Hindu

around.headline: Namma Metro passengers facing long queues at security checks
around.summary: Riders reported extended waits at entry security checkpoints today, per The Siasat Daily. Build in a few extra minutes if you're catching the metro this evening, especially at busier interchange stations.

around.headline: Karnataka bans selfies and reels, caps college educational tours at five days
around.summary: The state government's new rule restricts filming trends on college trips and limits their duration, per Times of India. Relevant if you or a family member has an upcoming college tour planned.

around.headline: Trump signs Russia sanctions bill authorising tariffs of up to 100% on India and China
around.summary: The law ties fresh sanctions on Russia's oil trade to steep potential tariffs on countries including India, per Telegraph India. Bengaluru's export-heavy tech and manufacturing firms are among those watching closely for how this could raise costs or disrupt trade terms.

street_smart.title: You're withdrawing cash at a standalone Bengaluru ATM late in the evening. The card slot feels slightly loose and there's a thin plastic attachment near the keypad you don't remember from your last visit. Your card is already halfway into the slot. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: No incident in today's feeds fits the choice-based trap format cleanly (today's real Bengaluru stories — a Lokayukta bribery sting, a child's abduction-murder over debt, road-repair disputes and a college-tour policy change — are corruption, tragedy or civic/administrative rather than a personal decision point). Rotating in from the evergreen list: credit-card/ATM skimming, which does not appear as a street-smart scenario anywhere in the archive.
street_smart.situation: It's late, the ATM kiosk is otherwise empty, and pulling your card back out feels awkward when you're not fully sure anything is actually wrong.

choices.text: Pull your card back out without entering your PIN, avoid touching the keypad further, and report the machine to your bank's card helpline before using a different ATM.
choices.feedback: Correct. A loose slot or an unfamiliar attachment is exactly how skimmers copy your card's magnetic stripe, and a paired pinhole camera can capture the PIN — so the safest move is to withdraw before either step completes and let the bank flag the machine.

choices.text: Go ahead and complete the withdrawal since you're already halfway through and nothing else seems unusual.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A skimmer's whole design relies on the transaction looking and feeling completely normal — by the time you notice anything, your card's stripe and PIN may already be captured, and fraudulent withdrawals can follow within hours.

choices.text: Cover the keypad with your other hand while entering your PIN and finish the transaction as usual.
choices.feedback: Risky. Covering the keypad guards against a hidden camera reading your PIN, but it does nothing about a compromised card slot — the stripe can still be cloned the moment the card goes in, regardless of how carefully you shield the keypad.

choices.text: Ask a stranger waiting nearby to glance at the machine and confirm whether it looks safe before you continue.
choices.feedback: Risky. This swaps one unverified risk for another — you have no way to know if that person is trustworthy, and their opinion doesn't actually remove a skimming device if one is fitted.

takeaways: If a card slot feels loose or you spot an unfamiliar attachment near the keypad, withdraw your card without entering your PIN and try a different, preferably branch-attached, ATM.
Report a suspicious machine immediately to your bank's 24x7 card helpline — banks can block and reissue a card fast if you act before any fraudulent transaction goes through.

If money is ever debited after a suspicious ATM visit, block the card right away and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or call the national cyber fraud helpline 1930 — early reporting improves the odds of a reversal.

quiz.question: What did Bengaluru's Lokayukta police catch a Central GST Superintendent doing on camera today?
quiz.why: The Lokayukta is Karnataka's anti-corruption ombudsman body, set up specifically to investigate complaints against public servants like this one.

quiz.question: Karnataka's new rule for college educational tours caps the trip length at how many days?
quiz.why: The rule was introduced alongside a ban on filming selfies and reels during these tours, following safety concerns raised by such trends.

quiz.question: The US sanctions bill Trump signed today authorises tariffs of up to what percentage on India and China?
quiz.why: The bill ties the tariff threat to countries' continued purchases of Russian oil, putting pressure on major buyers like India to diversify their energy sourcing.

quiz.question: Which number is India's national helpline for reporting cyber fraud, including card and bank scams?
quiz.why: 1930 connects to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, which can flag a fraudulent transaction to banks quickly enough to sometimes freeze the money before it's withdrawn.

quiz.question: Which river supplies most of Bengaluru's piped drinking water, pumped in from roughly 100 km away?
quiz.why: Because Bengaluru sits on a ridge with no major river of its own, the city depends heavily on pumped Cauvery water and groundwater, which is part of why its supply is considered fragile.
